Hi @Megha Rathi

What the screenshot shows. The APIS navigation frame renders in full for Carlo Conty, including the Admin tab, while the content panel comes back empty. Session, authentication and location hierarchy are resolving. The failure is server side while rendering the audit form. This is not a platform outage and not a permission gate on this user.

Deployment matters here. NEXCOM is an on prem APIS customer, government, and we hold no access to their production data or servers. Only the nexcom-prep site is reachable from our side. Nothing we normally run for this symptom, a screen rebuild, a label cache reset or a database check, can be executed by Support on this tenant. Their Lead Applications Administrator, Milan Djordjevic, is the counterpart who can pull IIS and application logs. He worked RCS-28642 with David Beck on 28 August.

On the Meijer comparison. RCS-28449, Meijer, Secure not loading, was a Secure 5 platform issue restored by Engineering within 47 minutes on 18 August and tracked in the Secure 5 Issues channel. Different product, different hosting, different failure mode. It is not a precedent for this ticket.

Closer precedents, all on Secure rather than APIS, same failure shape. RCS-28139, Sportsman's Warehouse, all audit screens unreachable for all users, caused by BuildAllScreens running synchronously on the HTTP thread and hitting the 100 second edge timeout. RCS-28032, Vitamin Shoppe, NewAudit.aspx and AuditLog.aspx rendering with unresolved screen labels. RCS-28709, Stater Bros, intermittent blank screen, still without a confirmed root cause and without a linked ENG.

Working hypothesis, not confirmed. Carlo reported he was in the middle of updating the Annual Ops/Services Review template when it stopped opening. A form that fails to render only after an edit points at the saved definition of that template rather than at the environment.

What we need from NEXCOM to move this forward.

  1. Whether other audit templates open normally for the same users. If they do, the issue is scoped to Annual Ops/Services Review.

  2. What changed on that template on or before 10 September, and who saved it.

  3. IIS and application event logs from their APIS server for 10 September around 16:46 Eastern, plus the browser console and network trace captured while the blank page loads.

One constraint to set expectations internally. APIS is a legacy product with no ongoing development. If this turns out to be a corrupted template definition and we have no access to their environment, the practical path is for NEXCOM to restore the previous version of the template from their own backup.

The template editor opens for him. What does not open are the forms hanging off it. Thirteen forms sit under ANNUAL OPS/SERVICES REVIEW, one per year since 2019 plus four created for 2026, and only three of them load, IDs 577, 575 and 341. Still a working read, not a cause. I have asked him for the time the page holds before it goes blank, which is what separates a timeout from an immediate failure, and for which form he actually needs this year.

If the timing comes back near one hundred seconds this stops being configuration and goes to AALPS engineering through Matthew Kamminga, with the caveat that APIS carries no ongoing development.

","created":"2026-09-16T07:38:23.308-0400","updated":"2026-09-16T07:38:23.308-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"712020:9c60cf80-4b59-4d63-8e7f-e75980d4a367","displayName":"Carlo Conty"},"jsdPublic":true},{"id":"3359291","author":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"body":"

1. Environment and steps to reproduce

Environment: NEXCOM production, on prem, customer hosted. Host whqapisiis01.nexad.nexweb.us. Application path /apis270/, so this tenant runs the 270 UI, not 275. The Confluence page Modules by Client lists NEXCOM as 275 and is wrong or stale, last modified September 2019.

NEXCOM (NEX), reported 10 September 2026

  1. Sign in to APIS production as Carlo Conty, LP admin, Admin tab visible.

  2. Audit Center, Audit admin tab, Templates.

  3. Open template ANNUAL OPS/SERVICES REVIEW, code OPS/SERV. The template editor opens.

  4. In the Forms section, click form 2026 Annual Retail & Svcs Review( ID:576 ).

Expected: the form editor renders. Actual: the content frame goes blank immediately. The browser holds for 8 to 10 minutes and then raises Chrome's This page isn't responding prompt on new_docframe.asp. Screenshots attached by the customer on 16 September.

Ten of the fourteen forms under that template fail the same way. IDs 577, 578, 575 and 341 open.

2. Findings

  • verified by customer. The page holds 8 to 10 minutes before Chrome raises the unresponsive prompt. That is the browser render thread blocking, not an edge timeout returning an error.

  • verified by customer. Template reads Template deleted.0, so it is neither deleted nor expired.

  • verified by customer. Another large template, 2026 Annual Safety Compliance Audit, opens normally.

  • verified by me, 14 September, prep tenant nexcom-prep. The Audit module renders normally there. The template from this ticket does not exist in prep, so the hang itself cannot be reproduced here.

  • verified by me, 22 September, prep tenant. Admin, Labels, Edit, Label Selection lists the tenant's full label catalog in sequence. It goes AUDIT.STATUS.0, AUDIT.STATUS.2, AUDIT.STATUS.4. AUDIT.STATUS.1 and AUDIT.STATUS.3 are not in the table. They were never created for this tenant, this is not a cache or display problem.

  • unverified, from AI triage, listed so it is not re-explored. Form volume on the combined 2026 forms may drive the render failure. The forms that still open are the split parts, one is literally named Pt2.

3. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

I walked the Audit module end to end in nexcom-prep on 14 September with the shared support account, and captured each screen. The template in this ticket does not exist in prep, and prep carries a different dashboard and menu configuration from their production, so prep does not model their live setup or reproduce the hang itself.

Claude flagged the unresolved status label as worth checking directly against the tenant's label table rather than assuming a cache problem. I checked three things myself on 22 September. I ran Reset Label Cache in prep, it recompiled all eight configured languages cleanly in 11.03 seconds with no error, and the unresolved status label on the Home dashboard did not change afterward. I ran the Troubleshoot Labels control character checker, it returned over 150 defective entries with invalid characters or unassigned names, none of them AUDIT.STATUS, so that check covers a different defect category. I then opened the label catalog directly and confirmed AUDIT.STATUS.1 and AUDIT.STATUS.3 are absent from it. This is what I think is happening. Could someone evaluate whether a missing status label can make a synchronous form render hang rather than fail fast, and give me your thoughts.

Support cannot go further alone. NEXCOM is on prem and government. We hold no access to their production data or servers. A screen rebuild, a label cache reset and any database read are all out of reach there. Their Lead Applications Administrator is Milan Djordjevic, who worked https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28642 with David Beck on 28 August.

4. Ruled out. Do not repeat

Hypothesis

Refutation

Template deleted or expired

Reads Template deleted.0 with the filter off

Edge timeout at 100s, as in https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28139

The page holds 8 to 10 minutes, no 504 or 524 returned

User permission gate, as in https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28852

Carlo has the Admin tab and other templates open for him

Stale label cache

Reset Label Cache recompiled cleanly on 22 September, the missing status label stayed unresolved

5. Still open

  1. Confirm whether NEXCOM's production label table has the same gap for AUDIT.STATUS.1 and AUDIT.STATUS.3 as prep, and whether adding those two entries is safe as a standalone fix.

  2. Tell me what to request from Milan on the server side. IIS logs alone may not show this if a response is being returned and the browser itself is what stalls.

  3. Confirm whether splitting form 576 permanently is the path forward, or whether a fix exists for the combined form.

Priority Medium, opened 10 September. The customer has already worked around it by splitting the annual review into two audits and assigning those to locations, so they are not blocked. Form 576 is the one they intended to assign.

Routing note. Aimee's L3 procedure, Confluence RTS 478006902856, sends code and bug work to Under Engineering Review with Shandana Khan as assignee, and the ENG auto creates on the transition. AALPS is the engineering queue for Incident, Audit, Aspect legacy and APIS, and Matt Kamminga owns that area. On https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28212 Viraj Kansara wrote on 18 August that all APIS goes direct to Matt Kamminga, so I am naming him here alongside the standard transition.

Thanks for confirming that, and good to know 576 is not the only one you still need working this year. That helps me understand the size of what we are looking at.

I have one more thing I would like to try, and it is something only you can do from your side, since it has to happen on the actual page while it is failing.

Whenever you have a moment, before you click into form 576, could you open your browser tools first? In Chrome that is the F12 key, or a right click on the page and Inspect. Once that panel opens, there is a section called Elements, and a piece of code in there starting with the word frameset, with a short string of numbers separated by commas. If you double click that string, you can change a few of the zeros to something like 10, then click elsewhere to apply it.

After that, go ahead and open form 576 like you normally would. A few thin strips should show up around the edges of the screen that are usually hidden, and one of them may display something once the page starts loading.

If anything shows up in those strips, even if it looks like nothing useful to you, a screenshot of it would help a lot on my end.

No worries at all if this does not work cleanly on the first try. Happy to hop on a quick call and walk through it together if that is easier than typing it out.

Thanks again, Carlo.

Juan Martinez
Appriss Retail Support

Environment: production, on-prem NEXCOM tenant, APIS 270 UI. Repro steps on record in this ticket, 10 and 16 Sep. Live working session with the customer, 30 September, recording and HAR attached to the ticket at 15:34.

Findings

  • verified by me, live session, 30 Sep, from the HAR. The request for admin_config_form.asp?recID=576 got a response in 3.64s, then the server took 1268.2s, about 21.1 minutes, to stream the 1.19MB body. Total 1271.9s, status 200, not an error.

  • verified by me, same HAR. Two unrelated requests on the same browser session, evidence_download.asp and fetch_custom_css.asp, independently waited about 1268s for a server response and both resolved within seconds of the 576 request finishing.

  • verified by me, watching live. The browser stayed responsive, DevTools and Network kept updating. Server side stall, not browser render thread blocking as my earlier note assumed.

  • verified by me, live. Carlo mentioned he has a larger audit coming and expects the same behavior past some size threshold.

Troubleshooting performed

Claude parsed the HAR after the call and flagged the pattern across the three stalled requests. I ran the working session myself with the customer on 30 Sep and watched DevTools directly. Could someone evaluate whether admin_config_form.asp holds a session level lock while generating output for large templates, classic ASP serializes requests sharing a session, and whether that explains why unrelated requests from the same session stalled together. Also check whether the missing AUDIT.STATUS.1 and .3 labels from my 22 Sep note add a per field delay in a large combined form.

Ruled out

Hypothesis

Refutation

Browser render thread blocking

TTFB was 3.6s, the delay is server side receive, DevTools stayed responsive

Session cookie lost

Fresh incognito login straight to 576 still hung the same way, 23 Sep

Edge timeout at 100s

Holds over 21 minutes, ends in 200, no 504 or 524

Still open

  1. Does admin_config_form.asp hold a session lock while streaming, explaining why unrelated requests from the same session stall together.

  2. Why does generating this template take over 21 minutes server side when the first byte arrives in 3.6s.

  3. Does the missing AUDIT.STATUS label pair add per field delay here.

Customer asked for an ETA today, over two weeks since opened, flags a bigger audit that may hit the same wall. Priority review requested.
